posts.cooked:
I've got a few questions on titles in the Bloodsworn Colosseum. 

1. Some of the titles apply if event X happens in a turn. Does that title go to the target at the end of turn or as soon as the condition is satisfied. Example: Haka Rampages. He hits all non heroes. Then after hitting two hero targets he is eligible for "The Indiscriminant." Does he get that title and hence the +1 damage for hitting the remaining heroes or does he get it after his turn is done.

 

2. Another timing question. A hero destroys a fourth nonhero target in the same turn. This plays "Champion" from the title deck. Can the hero claim the title even though the title was not face up when the third target was destroyed?

 

3. Is there any flavor text that people know of for the titles? I really want to know what's going on in some of those pictures.

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
That's not how Omnitron's components work. The "variable" tracking the damage amount does not exist until the card tracking it enters play. Otherwise you end up with things happening like Atlantean Font of Power causing components to enter play and immediately destroy themselves.

To be consistent with that, you would not get the title.

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
It will not. The variable on it for "damage this round" starts counting the moment it enters play.

This also means that different components can have different perspectives on the matter. It's an unusual case, but... AFOP makes unusual things happen all the time.

Thinking about it a bit more - this could also happen with Combat Stance or Flame Barrier or whatnot, if Omnitron gets dealt damage before it plays a component on its turn. Same thing.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
In one round tells you that the damage has to occur in the same round, that once the Villain turn starts the counting resets to 0 damage.

It apparently is not designating that counting can be retroactive.

Which means "First time each turn" actually counts as "First time this card is aware of each turn".
